tagline: Prove the fix — with Tenable's own scan of exactly what you changed.
problem: After a patch, the finding stays open until the next scheduled scan reaches that host — days, sometimes weeks. Building a one-off verification scan by hand means picking plugins, targets, a scanner and a credential in the UI, waiting, syncing navi.db and then comparing before and after yourself.
does: Scan Confirmation starts from what you're doing: confirm a fix, scan new hosts, scan new hosts with an existing scan's settings, or re-run a scan. To confirm a fix it searches navi.db for what's open (by CVE, plugin or tag), plans the smallest set of `navi scan create` scans, checks everything that could go wrong, and — after one confirm — launches them, streams every navi command into a live window, waits, syncs navi.db and gives a result per host × plugin with the next step for anything undecided.

glance.caption: Scan Confirmation's At a glance: scans to launch, targets and plugins, assets excluded, open findings in the baseline, local-check plugins and whether a credential is set — then the verdicts once the scans finish.

capabilities: search navi.db by CVE, plugin or tag, see how many hosts have each finding open, pick the plugins — the hosts fill in for you. CISA KEV hands a CVE straight over.
one row per scan with its exact (masked) navi command — one plugin per scan, targets chunked, reuse of an identical earlier scan when there is one.

eleven numbered checks: gates, scanner online, credential exists, local checks need a credential, known plugin IDs, scan cap, no identical run going, navi.db not locked, no plugin + policy mix, agent-only assets.
navi exits 0 even when a start fails, so every launch is proven by a new run in Tenable's scan history and every stop by a status read; times come from Tenable, not the server clock.
the whole run — create, wait, sync, verify — is one job in the same CLI window Settings uses, with the credential and navi's printed payload masked.

first-match rules over the baseline and navi.db after a scoped sync (`--since` for state changes and `--days 1` for still-open findings); each verdict keeps the scan, run, before and after state and the login evidence. CSV export.

⚡ One-off scan: a new scan with no policy (navi's Basic Network Scan or Host Discovery), a saved policy, the policy of one of your latest enabled scans, or plugin IDs; send new hosts through an existing scan (its policy and scanner); or re-run a scan as-is. Same plan, confirm and live window; no sync, no verdicts.
how: Scan Confirmation drives `navi scan create` (which creates AND launches), `navi explore api` reads of the scan history and status, and `navi config update vulns` scoped to the plugins. Launching needs writes enabled, scan launch separately enabled (NAVI_SCAN_LAUNCH) and a confirm; stop, pause, resume, re-verify and deleting old confirmation scans are gated the same way. Runs, scans, verdicts and a hash-chained event log live in tag_jobs.db.
who: Remediation owners who need proof a patch landed, VM leads closing tickets, and scan engineers who want a verification scan without building it in the UI.
better: Remote Remediation deploys the fix; Scan Confirmation proves it. Inconclusive verdicts point to Scan Health for the credential problem, and the synced findings flow into SLA Tracker and Exposure Score.
different: every verdict is a rule over Tenable's data — the same input always gives the same answer.
a host the scan never reached, a local check without a login, or a result navi hasn't synced yet says so instead of guessing.
cta: Send Scan Confirmation after the fix — the scan is the proof.
